text:
Brock Nelson is 35, past 1,000 NHL games, and still one of the more useful centers in Colorado. Six goals and 13 points in 21 games is fine rather than spectacular, but his minutes have dipped by about two a night over the last ten games, and he scored just three times in that stretch. One of them came in Montreal on Nov. 14, where The Hockey News called him a "noted Habs killer."

The underlying picture is steady. The Avalanche get 55% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, and his finishing sits inside our talent range rather than above it. His goals have come at good moments, too: he's added about a win by our clutch measure, more than his chances alone would explain.

Evolving-Hockey had him in the 98th percentile among forwards for driving offense last season, though alongside very strong teammates, and he was worth 2.0 wins while finishing below his chances. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking ranked him in the 96th percentile for chances from in front of the net. He's not the 33-goal scorer of last season so far. The ingredients for more are still there.
